page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.32xlarge is an enterprise-scale virtual instance within the Local SSDs family, designed to support memory-heavy and I/O-intensive workloads. Built upon KVM virtualization and standard x86_64 architecture, the server integrates 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Computational resources are coupled with 1024.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include GPU accelerators, focusing its silicon entirely on high-capacity memory handling and concurrent CPU execution.

A notable hardware differentiator of the ecs.i4r.32xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 7679 GB of direct-attached solid-state drive (SSD) capacity. This local configuration circumvents network-attached storage latency, delivering high input/output performance directly on the physical host. Complementing the internal storage architecture, the server provides 64 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, which supports heavy inter-node communication and data synchronization across large distributed server clusters. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From an efficiency perspective, the aggregation of massive memory capacity and local SSD hardware into a single instance provides high resource density, reducing management overhead for memory-constrained platforms compared to smaller scale-out nodes. However, relying on local ephemeral SSD storage requires external replication or persistent backup architectures to protect against node failures. The architectural combination of 128 vCPUs, 1024 GB RAM, and low-latency local storage makes ecs.i4r.32xlarge suited for high-scale in-memory databases, distributed key-value stores, real-time analytics platforms, transactional relational databases, and enterprise ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4r.32xlarge is a memory-optimized and storage-dense virtual server designed for demanding enterprise workloads. Operating on a KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system integrates 1024.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory density ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 7679 GB of bundled local solid-state storage, eliminating the latency constraints of external disk volumes for I/O-intensive operations. Network capabilities are provisioned with a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, ensuring robust throughput for distributed clustering and node replication. With no discrete GPU acceleration, the hardware allocation prioritizes raw compute parallelism, immense memory capacity, and low-latency storage. The instance serves workloads including distributed in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, transactional enterprise databases, and high-throughput real-time data processing engines.
